finalists.label: Multibacillary leprosy
finalists.why: It has the most specific evidence, including numerous acid-fast bacilli present and gradual hair loss, which are unique to this condition.

finalists.label: Lupus
finalists.why: It has a mix of systemic and specific findings, including swelling and painful hand joints, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and uveitis, which are not fully explained by other candidates.

finalists.label: Leprosy
finalists.why: It is supported by the presence of numerous acid-fast bacilli and gradual hair loss, which are distinctive features of this disease.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of numerous acid-fast bacilli and the combination of skin, joint, and hair loss symptoms make Multibacillary leprosy the most comprehensive explanation for the patient's condition.

support_spans: Multiple asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms for 40 days
Diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis (hematoxylin-eosin stain)
Numerous acid-fast bacilli present (acid-fast stain)
Fundus fluorescein angiography showed uveitis
contradict_spans: No previous infections, family history, or personal medical history of autoimmune diseases or psoriasis

support_spans: Swelling and painful hand joints for 13 months
Rheumatoid factor: 70.1 IU/mL (significantly elevated)
X-ray and joint ultrasound showed: osteoarthritis, synovitis, flexor tendon tenosynovitis, and bone erosions
contradict_spans: No decreased sensation to pain, temperature and/or touch
No previous infections, family history, or personal medical history of autoimmune diseases or psoriasis
